# i18n: from a text-keyed catalog to a generated byte blob

**Status:** design + prototype. The prototype (one real domain, end to end) is on this branch; the
migration plan in §7 covers the rest. Nothing here is a big-bang rewrite: every step leaves the tree
green and is independently revertible.

**Scope.** `internal/i18n`, its 10 `table_*.go` catalogs, the four `msg`/`T` facades that render
through them (`internal/lang/localizer.go:30`, `compiler/msg.go:17`,
`compiler/internal/cgen/localizer.go:17`, and `qkparser`'s own `msg`), and the coverage/ratchet tests
in `internal/i18n/coverage_test.go`.

**Everything below was re-verified on `origin/main` = `7e8e366`.** Claims that could not be verified
are marked ⚠ and listed in §9.

---

## 1. Architecture today

```
  call site            catalog (consumer, in-repo)                rendering
  ─────────            ───────────────────────────                ─────────
  msg("…中文…", a) ──┐
  msg("English…", a) ─┤   table_<domain>.go
  T("…", a)          ├──►  map[string]string                Localizer.T
  errf(…, 1, "…")    │     key   = the message text          i18n.go:201-213
                     │     value = the other language          │
                     └──►  Load()  i18n.go:82-107             ├─ Lookup(tpl, lang)  map lookup
                           direction = Han sniff on the KEY   │    i18n.go:126-133
                           i18n.go:220-237                    └─ fmt.Sprintf(format, args…)
                                                                   (Go string, every call)
```

Three properties follow from "the key is the text": the pairing between a message and its
translation is *the text itself*, the source language is *a property of the script the key is
written in*, and the set of messages is *whatever a source scanner can find*. Each of the six
defects below is one of those three properties failing in production.

---

## 2. Diagnosis, with evidence

Every row was checked against the tree, not inherited from the brief.

### D-1 — the catalog is keyed by the message text itself ✔ verified

| Evidence | What it shows |
|---|---|
| `internal/i18n/i18n.go:70` — `domains map[string]map[string]string // domain -> template -> translation` | the map key *is* the rendered template |
| `internal/i18n/i18n.go:126-133` — `Lookup(template string, l Lang)` | the only lookup entry point is by text |
| `internal/i18n/table_lexer.go:7` — `"实名结构体必须写 type：type struct { ... } %s;": "a named struct requires 'type': …"` | the Chinese text is the key |
| `internal/i18n/i18n.go:201` — `func (L Localizer) T(template string, args ...any) string` | call sites hand over the text they want translated |

**Consequence 1 — rephrasing silently drops the translation.** Fix an English typo at the call site
and the key no longer matches; `Lookup` misses, `T` returns the template verbatim
(`i18n.go:204-208`), and the user silently gets the *source* language. Nothing fails at compile
time. The property "every message has a translation" is therefore a property of *the current
spelling*, not of the message.

**Consequence 2 — identical text in two contexts is one entry.** Two contexts that happen to use the
same wording share bytes in `byKey` (`i18n.go:90-95`). `TestCatalogIntegrity`
(`coverage_test.go:172-188`) rejects the same template in *two domains* (`:179-181`) but not twice
inside one domain, and not at two call sites — and it cannot express "these two identical strings
are two messages that may need to diverge". There is no ID to attach a context, a translator note,
or a length limit to.

### D-2 — two source languages coexist, and direction is inferred by sniffing for Han ✔ verified

```
  i18n.go:220-227   needsTranslation(s) = "does s contain a Han rune?"
  i18n.go:232-237   sourceLang(tpl)     = ZH if needsTranslation(tpl) else EN
  i18n.go:96-102    Load(): the branch that decides which language gets the key
                    and which gets the value is that same sniff
```

Direction is not data; it is *inferred from the script of the key*. `internal/i18n/table_lexer.go`
shows both families living in one table — 13 Chinese-source entries (`:7-19`) and one English-source
entry (`:23`).

**This inference produced a real, shipped defect twice in one day** (2026-10-10):

| Commit | Defect | Why the design allowed it |
|---|---|---|
| `6a37193` "read each catalog entry's direction off its key" | `Load` indexed every table as if the key were Chinese, so **every English-source message rendered its Chinese value under `QK_LANG=en`** — CI caught it as `limits_test.go:61: diagnostic does not name the limit: "CompileError: 表达式嵌套深度超过本实现的 65536 层上限…"` | the direction existed only as an implicit convention about keys, so an index could be built the wrong way round and still type-check |
| `43bbff6` "consult the catalog for the localizer's language, not only EN" | `T` gated the lookup on `L.Lang() == EN`, so **105 migrated messages returned the raw call-site template under `QK_LANG=zh`** — the translation existed and was never reached | "which language is this message written in?" was answered by inspecting the text at the point of use, and the two use sites answered it differently |

**The ratchet is a symptom, not a policy.** `coverage_test.go:269-290`:
`const allowed = 318 // lowered by the English-source batches`. Measured today: **277** Chinese-source
wired templates (`go test ./internal/i18n/ -count=1 -v` → `coverage_test.go:289: Chinese-source wired
templates: 277 (limit 318)`), matching the brief exactly. A numeric ceiling on "how many messages are
written in the wrong language" exists *only* because the catalog cannot say which language an entry is
in. In the proposed design the same fact is a column in the source file, and the ceiling is 0 by
construction (§5).

### D-3 — no stable message IDs, so nothing is checked at compile time ✔ verified

There is no identifier for a message anywhere in the pipeline. `Lookup` takes text
(`i18n.go:126`), `Has` takes text (`i18n.go:136`), `Untranslated` takes a `[]string` of text
(`i18n.go:283`). The nearest thing to a check is `TestTemplatesRegistered`
(`coverage_test.go:124-146`), which is a **runtime** map lookup driven by a hand-maintained list of
function names:

```
  coverage_test.go:35-38   var templateIndex = map[string]int{
                               "T": -1, "Msgf": -1, "msg": -1,
                               "errf": 1, "warn": 2, "errAt": 0, "replyErr": 2,
                           }
```

A call whose callee is not in that list is not scanned; a call whose template argument is not a
`BasicLit` is skipped (`coverage_test.go:79-82`); a template reached through a helper is invisible.
The gate is "the literals we could see have entries", not "every ID has a value in every shipped
language". Also note `errf`, `warn`, `errAt`, `replyErr` appear in `templateIndex` but have no
definition anywhere in the tree (verified: `grep -rn "func errf\|func warn\|func errAt\|func replyErr"
internal compiler cmd` → no matches), so that half of the table is dead scanner configuration.

### D-4 — coverage is enforced by ratchets plus runtime counting, and the scanner cannot see the pinned parser module ✔ verified — the worst of the six

`github.com/QuarkLangCommunity/QuarkLangQkparser` is pinned by pseudo-version in `go.mod` and again in
`compiler/go.mod`. Its 30 `msg(...)` templates are the parser's user-facing diagnostics. The scanner
walks the repository root, and stops at any directory that contains `.git`:

```
  coverage_test.go:44   root := filepath.Join("..", "..")
  coverage_test.go:48   filepath.Walk(root, …)
  coverage_test.go:357-363  skipNestedRepo(): a directory with a .git ends the walk
  coverage_test.go:56-59    only *.go inside that walk is parsed
```

The parser module's source is not under the root and not under a sibling checkout in a normal clone —
it is inside the module cache (`$GOMODCACHE/github.com/!quark!lang!community/!quark!lang!qkparser@…`).
**It is unreachable by construction.**

Consequence, and this is the hole the brief calls out: **add a new `msg("…")` template to the pinned
parser module and it ships untranslated in every language with nothing failing.** The runtime counter
cannot help — a template with *no* catalog entry and *no* Han characters falls back to itself
(`i18n.go:201-213`) and is not even counted as a miss, because `sourceLang(template) == lang` for an
English-source template under EN (`i18n.go:206`). Under `QK_LANG=zh` it renders English text: the
exact user-visible failure this project spent two commits fixing in one day, with no gate at all.

Demonstrated, not asserted — see §6, proof P4.

### D-5 — rendering is a map lookup carrying Go strings ✔ verified

| Evidence | Cost |
|---|---|
| `i18n.go:71` — `byKey map[string]map[Lang]string` | one hash of the whole message **text** per render, two map probes |
| `i18n.go:89-103` — `Load()` builds a `map[Lang]string` per template | per-message heap objects: 1 nested map per message (566 messages today) |
| `i18n.go:212` — `fmt.Sprintf(format, args...)` | the format string is a Go string, re-parsed by `fmt` on every render |
| `i18n.go:96, 206, 232` — `needsTranslation` scans the template rune by rune | Unicode work on the hot path, per render |
| `miss.go:13-20` — a `sync.Mutex`-guarded `map[string]int` | a lock plus a string-keyed map on the fallback path |

`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` states the project's ordering as **bytes > structs > strings**; this path is
strings (twice over: a string key and a string value) with a map in the middle. Nothing about a
message needs a name at runtime: a message is an index into a translation table, and the table is
fixed at build time.

### D-6 — the catalog lives in the consumer while the templates live in the syntax layer ✔ verified

`qkparser/localizer.go:5-7` states the split explicitly:

> *"the syntax layer keeps its templates as the catalog keys and hands them to whichever localizer is
> installed, so this package never depends on a message catalog of its own."*

and `internal/lang/localizer.go:32-34` re-injects the consumer's localizer into the module:

```go
// The syntax layer renders its messages through the same localizer as the rest of this package, so
// the parser templates keep resolving against the catalog even though they now live in qkparser.
func init() { qkparser.SetLocalizer(langLocalizer) }
```

This *works* at runtime and is a reasonable dependency-avoidance move, but it moves the interface
boundary to the wrong side of the information: the module that owns the templates cannot check its
own message surface, and the consumer that owns the catalog cannot enumerate the module's templates
(§D-4). The guarantee is therefore **not compositional**: "this module's messages are all
translatable" is not a property `qkparser` can hold, and "this catalog covers the module I pin" is
not a property the consumer can hold. A new template in the module is unverifiable from both ends.

### 2.1 Summary

| # | Defect | Root property | Gate today | Severity |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| D-1 | text is the key | pairing = spelling | none | high |
| D-2 | direction sniffed from Han | source language = script | ratchet ≤318 (actual 277) | high — shipped twice |
| D-3 | no stable IDs | identity = text | runtime map + name list | high |
| D-4 | module templates unscannable | set = what the scanner sees | none | **worst** |
| D-5 | map lookup, Go strings | — | none | medium |
| D-6 | catalog in consumer, templates in module | — | none | high (cause of D-4) |

---

## 3. The design

The owner's prescription is followed literally: **a config/table file is the source, a generator packs
it into code at build time, and the runtime reads one contiguous byte blob through an offset table
addressed by stable constants.**

### 3.1 Shape

```
  AUTHORED SOURCE (the single source of truth)
    internal/i18n/source/<domain>.tsv        one row per (id, lang): strict, diffable, no escaping games
    internal/i18n/source/languages.tsv       the shipped languages, in order; the order is the index
                     │
                     │  cmd/qki18n  (§3.6) — stdlib only, deterministic, no go.mod additions
                     ▼
  GENERATED, COMMITTED
    internal/i18n/msg_<domain>_gen.go
       type Msg uint16                                    stable ID, not a string
       const MsgLexerNamedStructNeedsType Msg = 0         authored in the source file, frozen forever
       var msgOffsets = [...]uint32{ 0, 41, … }           end offsets into the blob
       var msgBlobEN  = "…"                               one contiguous byte blob per language
       var msgBlobZH  = "…"
                     │
                     ▼
  CALL SITE                          RENDER
    L.Msg(i18n.MsgLexerNamedStructNeedsType, a)   →   msgOffsets[id] ▸ language slice ▸ string
                                                      no map, no hash, no per-message object
```

The runtime value of a message is an integer. The only bytes are the blob. The only lookup is an
array index.

### 3.2 Stable IDs

An ID is authored, not derived, and is never recycled:

```
  lexer.named_struct_needs_type        # dotted: <domain>.<snake_case>
  lexer.anon_interface_no_generics
  parser.nesting_too_deep
```

* **Renaming the English text does not touch the ID.** This is property P1 (§6).
* **The generator assigns the numeric value** from the ID's position in the source file, and the
  source file is append-only by convention; `cmd/qki18n -check` fails if an existing ID's number
  changed (that is the one thing that must never happen silently, because the numbers index the blob).
* **Same text in two contexts is two IDs.** Nothing dedupes by text; two rows with identical `text`
  and different `id` are two messages that may diverge tomorrow.
* The ID *is* the translator's handle: context, a note, and a length budget are columns (§3.7), so the
  information D-1 destroyed has somewhere to live.

### 3.3 Direction is metadata, never a sniff

```tsv
# languages.tsv   lang  direction            (index = row order, 0-based)
en      source
zh      translation
```

`en` is the source language and must be listed first. No code inspects a template for Han characters
any more; `needsTranslation` and `sourceLang` (`i18n.go:220-237`) are deleted. "Which language is
this message written in" becomes a property of the *file*, and a message's rendering for a language is
simply `blob[lang][id]` — so the two defects of §D-2 cannot be expressed, let alone shipped:

* there is no index to build the wrong way round: the blob *is* the index;
* there is no "fall back to the source language" branch to gate on `EN`: every ID has a value in
  every shipped language, or the build fails (§3.4).

The ≤318 ratchet is deleted, not lowered: its subject (a message whose source language is ambiguous)
no longer exists.

### 3.4 Compile-time completeness, across the module boundary

Three layers, in increasing strength.

**(a) Generator-refuses.** `cmd/qki18n` exits non-zero if any ID is missing any shipped language. The
error names the ID and the language:

```
i18n: 1 message is incomplete:
  lexer.named_struct_needs_type: no "zh" row (languages.tsv ships en, zh)
```

**(b) Consumer-side staleness.** The generated file is committed, and
`TestGeneratedCatalogIsCurrent` re-runs the generator in memory and compares it byte for byte with
what is on disk. Any change to a template, an ID or a translation that was not regenerated fails
`go test ./... -count=1` — the ordinary gate.

**(c) The pinned parser module.** This is how the compositional hole (D-4, D-6) is closed, and it is
the part worth stating precisely.

```
  qkparser (pinned module, its own repository)
    i18n/source/*.tsv          ← the module OWNS its message IDs and its English text
    i18n/messages_gen.go       ← generated by the module's own `go generate`
        type ID uint16
        const IDNestingTooDeep ID = 0
        func Messages() []Message     // {ID uint16, Template string}, English, in ID order
                                     // Template keeps its fmt verbs: "%d" placeholders intact

  consumer (this repository), at `go generate ./internal/i18n`
    cmd/qki18n:
      1. reads   internal/i18n/source/*.tsv                      (its own messages)
      2. runs    go list -f {{.Dir}} <the pinned qkparser version>  → the module source directory
         reads   <that dir>/i18n/source/*.tsv                    (the module's authored source)
      3. checks  every (id, language) pair the module declares has a row in the consumer's zh columns
                 → else: the GENERATOR FAILS, before any code exists to compile
      4. emits   one Msg constant + one blob slot for the union of both ID sets
```

Why this closes the hole, in one sentence: **the module publishes its ID set as data that the
consumer's build step consumes, so a template the module ships but the catalog does not cover is a
generation failure in the consumer's tree — not a runtime fallback in a user's terminal.**

Three properties make it hold rather than merely look right:

1. **The module's IDs are the module's data.** It does not import the consumer, keep a stateful
   registry, or need a post-`init` hook — the same reason the current `SetLocalizer` injection could
   be removed rather than extended.
2. **The pin is the version.** Step 2 reads the module *at the version `go.mod` pins*. Move the pin to
   a module revision that added a template, and step 3 sees the new ID on the next generation and
   fails until the catalog covers it. So "a new template in the module ships untranslated" is now
   caught by the ordinary `go generate` + `go test` loop, on all three CI platforms, with no new job.
3. **The consumer's catalog stays self-contained at runtime.** Values are baked into the consumer's
   blob; the binary does not read the module's source, and `qkparser` still depends on nothing.

Step 3 is by design **not** a Go-level import of the module into the consumer's `i18n` package: a
generator that reads a pinned module's source directory keeps the runtime dependency graph unchanged
(`internal/i18n` staying independent of the parser is what lets the catalog be used from `cmd/qkdoc`,
`cmd/qklsp` and tests without pulling the parser in). If a future review prefers a hard compile-time
coupling, the same data supports `qkparser.Messages()` being imported by `cmd/qki18n` instead of read
from disk — the check is the same check, only the transport differs. ⚠ Deliberate, reversible choice;
§9.

### 3.5 The blob

Per language, one contiguous byte blob and one `uint32` end-offset table:

```
  msgBlobEN = "the concatenation of every English template, in ID order, no separators"
  msgOffsets[k] = end offset of message k (exclusive); start = msgOffsets[k-1] (0 for k = 0)

  msgOf(id, lang)  →  msgBlob[lang][ offsets[id-1] : offsets[id] ]  →  string(...) — one slice
```

* No separators: the offset table carries the boundaries, so a message may contain any byte including
  NUL and newline.
* `unsafe.String`/`[]byte` aliasing would make the zero-copy property explicit; the prototype uses a
  plain slice expression instead, which does not allocate because the blob is a constant string. No
  `unsafe` is introduced. ⚠ The allocation count is argued from the shape of the code, not measured
  (§9).
* The `"%d"` verbs stay in the blob, so `fmt.Sprintf` is still called for messages with arguments —
  the prototype keeps byte-identical output including `fmt`'s `%!x(…)` diagnostics on bad calls. What
  disappears is the *lookup*, the *fallback branch*, the *Han scan* and the *miss counter*.
* Order is the source file's order, so the blob is byte-stable across machines and Go versions and
  diffs are readable in review.

### 3.6 The generator

`cmd/qki18n`, in-repo, stdlib only (no dependency is added to any `go.mod`):

| Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| *(none)* | write the generated files |
| `-check` | regenerate in memory and compare with what is on disk; non-zero on drift |
| `-strict` | treat a missing language as an error (the default; the flag exists so the failure can be demonstrated in a test, and so a legacy domain can be migrated before it is complete) |

Wire-up: `//go:generate go run ../../cmd/qki18n` in `internal/i18n`. Output is committed (the brief's
requirement, and the reason `go build ./...` never needs the generator to run). Determinism: no
timestamps, no map iteration, author order only; verified by generating twice and comparing
(§6, P2).

### 3.7 The authored source file

```
# internal/i18n/source/lexer.tsv
# id                            ctx     note                                   en                                    zh
lexer.named_struct_needs_type   parse   named types need 'type' before struct   "a named struct requires 'type': type struct { ... } %s;"  "实名结构体必须写 type：type struct { ... } %s;"
```

Columns: `id`, `ctx` (the collision-killer D-1 lacked), `note` (translator context), then one column
per language in `languages.tsv` order, `strconv.Quote`d so `\n`, `\t` and quotes are lossless. Row
granularity is one *language*, so a missing translation is a missing row — the most diffable shape and
the easiest to check. Format choice: TSV rather than TOML/YAML/JSON, because the repository's stated
principle is "no third-party dependencies" (the toolchain depends on nothing outside itself) and
because a quoted TSV row is one line per message per language in review. ⚠ If a future editor wants
richer structure, the format is the generator's private contract — a Go-literal source, already read
with `go/ast` elsewhere in the repo (`coverage_test.go:66-99`), is the obvious substitute.

### 3.8 Interface change at the call site

```go
// today
msg("实名结构体必须写 type：type struct { ... } %s;", name)

// after
L.Msg(i18n.MsgLexerNamedStructNeedsType, name)
```

`Localizer.T`/`i18n.T` remain during the migration as a deprecated shim that resolves text → ID via a
generated reverse table, so a domain can be migrated without touching every call site in one commit.
The shim is itself deleted at the end of the migration (§7, step 5): what makes D-3 unfixable today is
that a text entry point exists at all.

---

## 4. What the ratchets become

| # | Ratchet today | Proposed fate |
|---|---|---|
| R-1 | untranslated templates ≤124 → now 0 (`coverage_test.go:134`) | **deleted** — replaced by generator-refuses (§3.4a), which fails before a file exists rather than counting afterwards |
| R-2 | Chinese-source ≤318, actual 277 (`coverage_test.go:270`) | **deleted with a proof**: after the migration the count is 0 by construction (direction is a column). The retirement lowers 318 → `len(wired)` and then removes the test, with one intermediate step where it is asserted to be 0 |
| R-3 | direct `i18n.T(` call sites ≤29, actual 25 (`coverage_test.go:243`) | **kept, then strengthened**: the shim must not grow, and the test flips from "≤29 `i18n.T(`" to "0 text-keyed entry points" — it becomes an exact contract |
| — | `TestTemplatesRegistered` (scanner-based) | **deleted last**, once no call site passes text. It is the test that says "the scanner cannot see the module" (§D-4); it has no meaning after IDs |
| — | `TestNoSilentFallback` / `Misses` / `miss.go` | **deleted**: with total completeness there is no fallback to count. The miss counter is the *mechanism for tolerating* the defect. ⚠ Until the last domain migrates, both must coexist — the counter keeps its meaning for unmigrated domains and keeps its zero assertion |
| — | `TestCatalogIntegrity`, `TestVerbSetsMatch`, `TestVerbSequenceMatches` | **kept, re-pointed at the generated data** — they are good tests; only the source of truth moves from Go maps to the TSV |

Nothing is deleted before the thing that replaces it is green. R-2 in particular is only removed
*after* the count reaches 0, so the ratchet is not retired on a promise.

---

## 5. Non-goals

* **Not a big-bang rewrite.** One domain per commit; both mechanisms live side by side until the last
  domain moves.
* **Not a translator-facing tool.** The design makes a translator's job *possible* (context, notes, no
  text-as-key), not *pleasant*: no TMX/XLIFF export, no plural rules, no per-locale variant selection.
  Those are additive on top of IDs and belong in a later design.
* **Not `unsafe`.** Byte-level rendering means "no map, no per-message object", not "no Go string".
* **Not a new dependency.** No `go.mod` change in either repository.
* **Not a change to `spec/STANDARD.md`, `compiler/testdata/compare.sh`, or the language surface.**
  User-visible output is a *constraint* here: it must not change.

---

## 6. The prototype: proof

Domain: **the pinned syntax layer's `msg()` surface — 24 messages — plus the parser's nesting refusal
(25 IDs in total)**. It is the honest choice rather than an easy one: these are exactly the messages the
scanner cannot see (§D-4), one of them is the English-source entry whose direction the `6a37193`
inversion got wrong, and the prototype covers the whole loop across a repository boundary — the module
authors the table, this repository's build reads it, checks it, packs it and renders it.

### 6.0 Reproduce

```sh
git switch feat/i18n-generated-catalog
go generate ./internal/i18n           # regenerates the committed catalog (a no-op when current)
go test ./internal/i18n/ -count=1 -v  # the proofs below, plus the pre-existing coverage and ratchets
internal/i18n/proof/byte_identical.sh # P3, end to end against origin/main
go test ./... -count=1                # the whole tree
```

| Property | Test / command | Where |
|---|---|---|
| P1 rephrasing does not lose the translation | `TestProofRephraseKeepsTranslation` | `internal/i18n/proof_test.go` |
| P1, the mirror (what the old design does) | `TestProofTextKeyedCatalogLosesTheTranslationOnRephrase` | same |
| P2 a missing language fails the build | `TestProofMissingLanguageFails` (25 message × language pairs), `TestGeneratedCatalogIsCurrent` | same |
| P2 across the module boundary | `TestProofModuleMessageIsCompleteInThisCatalog`, `TestModuleIDsAndCatalogIDsAgree` | same |
| P3 byte-identical output, `en` and `zh` | `internal/i18n/proof/byte_identical.sh` | `internal/i18n/proof/` |
| P4 the runtime reads the blob | `TestProofRuntimeReadsTheBlob`, `TestProofMigratedMessagesAreNoLongerMapEntries` | `internal/i18n/proof_test.go` |
| determinism | `TestGeneratedCatalogIsDeterministic` | same |

### 6.1 P1 — rephrasing an English message does not lose its translation ✔

`TestProofRephraseKeepsTranslation` rewrites the English text of `parser.macro_needs_name` in the
authored table, regenerates **in memory**, and then reads the result the way the runtime does: it parses
the regenerated file's `msgOffsets` and `msgBlob` and slices out the value for that ID in each language
block. The English changes; the Chinese is byte-identical and still addressed by the same constant.

The mirror test is what makes that a measurement. It builds the catalog the old way — call-site Chinese
as the key, English as the value, which is literally what `internal/i18n/table_macro.go` did before this
branch deleted the row — and applies the same rephrase:

```
text-keyed catalog, QK_LANG=zh, after the rephrase → "ParseError: a macro declaration needs a name, line 1"
```

A Chinese reader gets English. And the miss counter that is supposed to catch exactly this fires **only
under `zh`**: under `en`, `sourceLang` reads the rephrased text as English, the requested language
matches, and the loss is recorded nowhere (`i18n.go:206,220-237`). The test asserts both behaviours. So
"the gate notices a dropped translation" was, for an English-source message, true only for one of the
two languages — and the silently-unnoticed half is the one a Chinese reader hits.

### 6.2 P2 — omitting a language for one ID fails the build ✔

* **Structural.** In `parser.tsv`, a language is a *column*. A row that lost its `zh` value cannot be
  written down: the generator's row parser requires an exact column count and reports
  `want 7 tab-separated columns, got 6 (a missing language is a missing column)`.
* **Behavioural.** `TestProofMissingLanguageFails` does not stop at one sample. It walks **every**
  (message, language) pair in the real table, drops that one value, and asserts that (a) the
  completeness check reports it naming the message, and (b) `Run` writes no file at all. It logs
  `checked 25 (message, language) pairs: every one fails generation when its value is removed`.
* **Standing.** `TestGeneratedCatalogIsCurrent` regenerates in memory and compares with the committed
  file byte for byte, so a template, an ID or a translation changed without regenerating fails the
  ordinary `go test ./... -count=1`. `TestGeneratedCatalogIsDeterministic` generates five more times and
  compares, because the message *numbers* are positions: a generator that walked a map — which this one
  did before the proof caught it — would renumber the whole blob run to run.

### 6.3 P2 across the module boundary — the hole closed ✔

This is the claim §3.4 exists for, and it is checked in both directions by
`TestProofModuleMessageIsCompleteInThisCatalog`:

* **A message the module gains.** The pin decides which revision is read, so the module's table is the
  same file the module generates from. `CheckModule` iterates *the module's* messages and reports every
  ID no row here carries: `the pinned module ships this message and no row in this catalog carries it`.
  The test removes every imported row and asserts one problem per module message — 25 of them — which is
  the mechanical form of "a new `msg()` in the syntax layer cannot ship untranslated".
* **A message the module rephrases.** Every imported row records the module's text in a `src` column;
  a row whose `src` disagrees with the pinned revision is reported as
  `this repository records src "…" but the pinned module ships "…"`.
* **The IDs line up.** `TestModuleIDsAndCatalogIDsAgree` asserts that each imported message has the same
  number in the generated catalog as in the module's own table, which is what lets
  `internal/lang`'s bridge be a type conversion (`i18n.Msg(id)`) rather than a lookup table. It logs
  `25 imported messages share their number with the pinned module`.

**One design correction the prototype forced.** The obvious table shape — an `en` column that is both
the module's source text and this repository's English rendering — is wrong, and the byte-identical
prove caught it: 12 of these messages are *still written in Chinese* inside the module, so their `en`
column is a translation, not the source. Setting `en` to the module's text made `QK_LANG=en` print
Chinese again, which is precisely the `6a37193` inversion. The table therefore carries both columns:
`src` (what the module ships, checked against the pin) and one column per shipped language (what this
repository renders). They converge as the module migrates; the design does not assume they are equal,
and the byte-identical corpus is what would have caught the assumption.

### 6.4 P3 — rendered output is byte-identical to today's under `QK_LANG=en` and `QK_LANG=zh` ✔

`internal/i18n/proof/byte_identical.sh` builds the pre-migration interpreter from a detached worktree at
`origin/main`, builds this tree, and runs both over a corpus of one case per migrated message family —
the deep-nesting refusal, four preprocessor failures, two macro failures, and a program that must still
run — comparing `stdout + stderr + exit code` byte for byte:

```
$ internal/i18n/proof/byte_identical.sh
en  deep_nesting.qk          identical (160 bytes)
en  macro_missing_body.qk    identical (70 bytes)
en  macro_needs_name.qk      identical (51 bytes)
en  ok_program.qk            identical (7 bytes)
en  pp_elif_without_if.qk    identical (104 bytes)
en  pp_error_directive.qk    identical (97 bytes)
en  pp_insert_needs_ast.qk   identical (85 bytes)
en  pp_unclosed_if.qk        identical (110 bytes)
en  pp_unknown_command.qk    identical (85 bytes)
zh  … (the same nine)
all identical (interpreter: origin/main == this tree), en and zh  [18 runs]
```

### 6.5 P4 — the runtime reads the blob, not a map ✔

* `TestProofRuntimeReadsTheBlob` walks every (language, message) pair and asserts that the value the
  renderer returns is `msgBlob[msgOffsets[k]:msgOffsets[k+1]]` for the same `k` — 50 slices over 25
  messages in 2 languages, plus the offset table's length checked against `messages × languages + 1`.
  It then renders one message through a real `Localizer` in both languages and requires the two to
  differ, so "the language selects the block" is not a tautology.
* `TestProofMigratedMessagesAreNoLongerMapEntries` asserts the complementary fact: none of the 50
  rendered texts is a key in the text-keyed catalog. Logged:
  `the 25 generated messages are absent from the 542 text-keyed entries`.
* Rendering is one index and one slice. There is no hashing of message text, no `needsTranslation` scan
  over the template, no fallback branch and no miss counter on the migrated path — those functions still
  exist for the 542 unmigrated entries, and §4 says when they go.

### 6.6 What the prototype found that the diagnosis did not

Three defects surfaced while doing the work, none of which any gate reported:

| # | Finding | Evidence | Why nothing noticed |
|---|---|---|---|
| F-1 | **A syntax-layer message with no catalog entry at all.** `"%s:%d: #%s 没有对应的 #if"` (`qkparser/preproc.go:145`) is the one module template absent from the 566-entry catalog. Under `QK_LANG=en` a reader got Chinese; under `QK_LANG=zh` the same message could come out English for a Chinese reader. | cross-checking the module's `msg(` surface against the catalog: `23 of 24 registered, 1 missing` | `TestTemplatesRegistered` can only check wired → catalog, and the module is unwired; `TestNoSilentFallback` cannot see it either, because a template with no Han characters is not counted as a miss under EN at all (§D-4) |
| F-2 | **The catalog and the scanner disagree about what is wired.** 13 messages in `table_lexer.go` look wired to the scanner but are emitted by the syntax layer, so the scanner's "wired templates" (485) is neither the catalog size (566) nor the messages the module actually ships. The 277-strong R-2 ratchet is measuring a set that includes entries no call site can reach. | `wiredTemplates` (`coverage_test.go:42-106`) finds no call site for any of the 13; the templates come from `parser.go`, `macro.go`, `preproc.go` and `token.go` | the check is one-directional: catalog entries without call sites are never examined |
| F-3 | **The same message text lives in two tables and in two source languages.** `internal/i18n/table_lexer.go` and `table_typecheck.go:47` hold the parser's nesting refusal (the latter prefixed with `CompileError:`), and the module emits it again — three call paths, one wording, two directions, keyed by text. | the prototype's `-check` refuses to generate while any migrated rendering is still a text-keyed key | nothing compares a catalog entry to the module revision it came from |

F-1 is the defect the design's §3.4 check exists to make impossible, and it is now covered: the row for
`parser.pp_branch_without_if` carries its English and Chinese values, and the byte-identical run for
`pp_elif_without_if.qk` shows the reader now gets the same bytes as before *and* the entry exists.

## 7. Migration plan

One domain per step; each step is its own commit, and step 2 is its own pair of PRs. Green at every
point. Steps 0-2 are this branch.

| Step | Content | What breaks | Rollback |
|---|---|---|---|
| **0 ✔ done** | `cmd/qki18n`, `internal/i18ngen`, `source/languages.tsv`, generator tests. No call site touched. | nothing | revert the commit |
| **1 ✔ done** | Migrate the syntax layer's `msg()` surface: 25 rows in `source/parser.tsv`, `internal/i18n/msg_gen.go`, the module's own IDs and blob, the `Localizer` seam, `proof/byte_identical.sh`. | nothing observable: the 25 renderings removed from `table_macro.go`, `table_compiler.go` and `table_lexer.go` are byte-identical to the values the blob now carries, which the corpus checks | revert the commit; the tables come back with it |
| **2 ✔ done (module branch pushed)** | **qkparser** gains `i18n/source/messages.tsv`, `cmd/mkmsg`, `messages_gen.go` and the ID-based `Localizer`; this repository's generator reads that table at the pinned revision and checks its IDs. | the pin moves, so `compiler/go.mod` follows; **the module must merge first**, and the pin bump is the second PR | revert the pin bump. ⚠ A revision without `i18n/source/messages.tsv` makes `go list` succeed but `Load` fail on the missing file — a hard failure, which is the honest behaviour, but it means the pin and the module must move together. When the module's `Localizer` interface changed from text-keyed `T` to `Msg(ID, …)`, this repository's `internal/lang` had to change in the same commit: there is no deprecation window in the prototype, and the final design owes one (§9) |
| **3 ✔ done (module + consumer)** | The rest of the syntax layer: the `errf(…)` templates in `qkparser`, then this repository's 13 `table_lexer.go` messages, whose call sites are all in the module. Measured surface, not the estimate this row used to carry: **40 call sites, 38 distinct templates** — 13 written in Chinese and 25 English-only. See §7.2 and §7.3. | the module's `errf` becomes `errfID` and the two `errf` methods are deleted, so there is no text-keyed path left in the module; every `src` value in `parser.tsv` moves to its English text, and a `src` that no longer matches the pin fails generation — which is the intended coupling | per-commit revert |
| **4** | The eight in-repository domains: `shared` (1), `docgen` (7), `repl` (13), `lint` (22), `cli` (27), `runtime` (65), `typecheck` (142), `compiler` (252). One commit each, largest last. | each commit deletes that domain's rows; unmigrated domains keep working through `T` | per-domain revert |
| **5** | Delete the shim: `Localizer.T`, `i18n.T`, `Load`, `Catalog`, `miss.go`, the `table_*.go` files, and the retired ratchets (§4). Point `TestCatalogIntegrity`/`TestVerbSetsMatch` at the generated data. | any out-of-tree consumer of `i18n.T` — none: the package is `internal/`, so it is unreachable outside this module | revert |

### 7.1 What breaks at each step — the honest list

* **Step 2 is the only cross-repository step**, and the prototype did it for real: the module's branch
  `feat/generated-message-ids` changes an exported interface, so an old consumer of `qkparser` that
  calls `Localizer.T` stops compiling. That is deliberate — a text-keyed entry point is what makes D-3
  unfixable — but the final design owes a time-boxed deprecation window (§9).
* **`QK_LANG=zh` output must not change at any step.** Every step runs `proof/byte_identical.sh`
  extended with that domain's corpus. Migrating a domain moves *where* the text lives, never *which*
  text is chosen. This is also the check that caught the wrong table shape in §6.3.
* **Ratchets**: R-2 is lowered to the measured value in each step and deleted at step 5. It is never
  raised, and never lowered to a number that is not measured by the same run. Note that the prototype
  does **not** move R-2: it migrated 25 messages the scanner never counted (277 before, 277 after). R-2
  moves in steps 3-4, when the messages the scanner *can* see are the ones being migrated — and F-2 says
  the set it measures needs fixing before its number means anything.
* **The 277 Chinese-source entries are re-authored, not retranslated.** For each, the language columns
  are the existing translation and the existing key. The migration's real risk is transcription, and the
  mitigation is that mechanical column-by-column diff against the old table, plus the byte-identical
  corpus. The prototype's 25 rows were done exactly that way.
* **Duplicates must be removed, not shadowed.** While a message is in both the generated catalog and a
  `table_*.go`, the two modules disagree about where its text comes from. The prototype's
  `TestProofMigratedMessagesAreNoLongerMapEntries` is the guard: it fails if a migrated rendering is
  still a text-keyed key. It failed on this branch, on 23 rows, and they were deleted.
* **Reviewer cost.** Steps 3-4 are large mechanical diffs (~540 messages). They are deliberately boring
  and split by domain: no reviewer should have to hold two domains in their head.

### 7.2 F-1 is already fixed — and the leak that actually remains

F-1 was reported in §8 as "one module message has no catalog entry". That was true at `7e8e366`; it is
**not** true at `926d24a`. The prototype's step 1 migrated the whole 25-row `msg()` surface, and
`"%s:%d: #%s 没有对应的 #if"` is row 21 of `internal/i18n/source/parser.tsv`
(`parser.pp_branch_without_if`). Re-verified on the inherited revision by running the built
interpreter on `#else` and `#endif` with no open `#if`:

```
$ QK_LANG=en ./quark else.qk      error: else.qk:1: #else without a matching #if
$ QK_LANG=zh ./quark else.qk      error: else.qk:1: #else 没有对应的 #if
```

`qkparser/preproc.go:145` reaches it as `msgID(IDPpBranchWithoutIf, filename, i+1, m[1])`, so the
rendering goes through the consumer's catalog and both languages are correct. No change is owed here.

The leak that *is* live is the surface step 3 exists to move, and it is larger than "one message": the
module's `errf` path does not consult any localizer at all. `parser.go:71` and `token.go:196` are
`fmt.Sprintf(format, args...)`, so every `errf` call site renders its own literal in **both** languages,
and the consumer's `table_lexer.go` translations for those templates are unreachable:

```
$ QK_LANG=en ./quark func.qk
error: ParseError: 函数声明关键字是 fn：func main(...) 应写为 fn main(...) at line 1, col 1
$ QK_LANG=zh ./quark func.qk
error: ParseError: 函数声明关键字是 fn：func main(...) 应写为 fn main(...) at line 1, col 1
```

The `en` run and the `zh` run are byte-identical, and the English text
`the function keyword is 'fn': write fn main(...) rather than func main(...)` exists in the repository
but is never selected. Measured surface at `926d24a`:

| Quantity | Value |
|---|---|
| `errf(` call sites in `qkparser` (excluding the two definitions) | 40 |
| distinct `errf` templates | 38 |
| of those, Han-containing (dead `table_lexer.go` keys today) | 13 |
| of those, English-only (migrating *adds* coverage) | 25 |
| `errfID(` call sites before step 3 | 1 |

The scanner cannot see any of this, because the templates live in the pinned module rather than in this
repository, and the miss counter does not fire, because a template that renders identically in both
languages looks like a message that was never translated *from* anywhere rather than one that is
missing a translation.

A first pass counted 29 templates because the extraction pattern assumed `errf(tok, "…")` and the
lexer's nine are `lx.errf(line, col, "…")`. The count above comes from the conversion itself, which had
to name every call site, and 31 + 9 = 40 is what it found. The lesson is the same one §9 keeps making:
the number you get depends on the pattern you asked with.

### 7.3 What step 3 did, and the numbers either side of it

Two pull requests, module first: `QuarkLangQkparser#4` gives every `errf` call site an ID and the
module an English source, and this repository's pin bump carries the 63 IDs and deletes the 13 dead
`table_lexer.go` rows.

| Quantity | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `errf(` call sites in the module | 40 | 0 |
| `errf` methods in the module | 2 | 0 (deleted; a call site cannot name a text) |
| `errfID(` call sites | 1 | 41 |
| rows in the module's `i18n/source/messages.tsv` | 25 | 63 |
| of those, whose text is English | 1 | 63 |
| rows in `internal/i18n/source/parser.tsv` | 25 | 63 |
| text-keyed catalog entries | 542 | 529 |
| rows deleted from `table_lexer.go` | — | 13 |
| P2 `(message, language)` pairs that fail generation when dropped | 25 | 63 |
| P2 imported IDs checked against the pin | 25 | 63 |
| P3 corpus runs | 18 | 50 (8 of them a declared EN fix) |
| `TestEnglishSourceRatchet` (R-2) | 277 | 277 — **did not move; see §7.1** |
| `TestDecouplingRatchet` | 25 | 25 |
| imported rows whose `zh` repeats the source | 25 (uncounted) | 25, ratcheted by `TestProofUntranslatedImportsAreCounted` |

Three things the design did not predict, recorded rather than smoothed over:

1. **R-2 did not move, and so was not lowered.** §7.1 expected it to fall in step 3. It measures Han
   templates at call sites *in this repository*, and the 13 templates step 3 deleted had their call
   sites in the module, so the scanner never counted them: 277 before, 277 after. Lowering it to
   anything else would have been a number no run produced, which §7.1 forbids. The count it was taken
   for is now `TestProofUntranslatedImportsAreCounted`, which measures the catalog instead of the call
   sites and has a backlog to count.
2. **P3 cannot be byte-identical under `en` for the 13.** The whole point is that the English rendering
   changes: the reader stops getting Chinese. `proof/byte_identical.sh` therefore asserts identity under
   `zh` for every case and, under `en`, identity except for a table of eight declared fixes — and for
   those it checks the leak *and* the fix by name: the baseline's English run must contain the Chinese
   template and the new run must be the baseline's with that template replaced by the English text
   `table_lexer.go` already shipped, byte for byte and with no other change.
3. **`//go:generate` was never committed.** §3.4 and §8.1's run log both show
   `go generate ./internal/i18n`, but no file carried the directive, so it silently did nothing and the
   only way to regenerate was to know the command. Step 3 adds it
   (`internal/i18n/generate.go`), with the flags spelled relative to the package directory because that
   is where `go generate` runs the command.

The 25 English-only templates gained an ID and a row whose `zh` value repeats its `en` value. That is
deliberate and it is the honest state: they shipped English-only, there was no Chinese translation to
move, and inventing one would have changed what a Chinese reader sees, which P3 forbids. The difference
is that the gap is now a row in a table, an ID in the catalog and a number in a ratchet, instead of a
silent English string in a Go file two repositories away.

## 9. Tradeoffs and unverified points

**Tradeoffs, accepted:**

1. **Committed generated code** is a build artefact in review. It buys "the build never needs the
   generator to run" and makes the blob greppable in a diff. Mitigated by `-check` in the ordinary test
   run (`TestGeneratedCatalogIsCurrent`).
2. **The generator reads the pinned module's source directory** (`go list -m -f {{.Dir}}`), which couples
   generation to the module's *layout*, not just its API. It keeps `internal/i18n` free of the parser
   dependency — which matters, because `cmd/qkdoc`, `cmd/qklsp` and the i18n tests all use the catalog
   without the parser. The alternative (import `qkparser` in the generator) trades that for a harder
   guarantee on the module's *API*; both are supported by the same data, and §3.4 step 3 is where the
   choice is made.
3. **Two columns where one looks sufficient** (`src` and the language columns, §6.3). It is one column
   more than the design first proposed, and the prototype's byte-identical run is what justified it.
4. **A TSV row per (id, language)** inflates the file in exchange for "a missing translation is a
   missing column". One row per ID with a column per language is more compact and more
   merge-conflict-prone on the language axis; this shape conflicts on the message axis instead.
5. **The numeric ID is positional**, so inserting a row renumbers the blob; frozen by convention and by
   the append-only source file. A hash-derived ID would need an ID→index map, which is what this design
   removes.
6. **Text-keyed `T` survives during the migration**, so D-1/D-3 remain live for the 529 unmigrated
   entries. That is the deliberate price of not doing a big-bang rewrite.
7. **`errf` call sites were the second half of the module's surface, and step 3 closed it.** The 40 call
   sites now name IDs and the two `errf` methods are gone, so the module has one message path. 25 of the
   38 templates had no Chinese translation to move — they were English-only and rendered English under
   both locales — so their rows repeat the source in the `zh` column and
   `TestProofUntranslatedImportsAreCounted` freezes the backlog at 25. This is the one place where the
   migration deliberately leaves work behind, and it is now a number rather than a silence.

**Unverified / open — marked, not hidden:**

* ✔ **Step 2's real-world ordering** was done for real: the module merged first
  (`QuarkLangQkparser#3`) and this repository's pin followed, with the generated catalog unchanged by
  the bump. It was driven from one machine rather than by two teams, so the *social* ordering (who
  lands first, and who waits) is still untested.
* ⚠ **The `qkparser` interface break has no deprecation window.** Every consumer that calls
  `Localizer.T` stops compiling. Deliberate, but it is a compatibility promise this design changes, and
  the release plan for the module is not mine to set.
* ⚠ **No allocation measurement.** "No map, no per-message object" is argued from the shape of the code
  (one index, one slice over a constant string) and from the removal of `byKey`, not from `-benchmem`.
  A benchmark belongs with step 4, when the hottest call sites have migrated.
* ⚠ **Plural/quantity selection** is out of scope (§5) and unaddressed: a language that needs a
  different verb form per count cannot ship on this design as it stands (nor on the old one).
* ⚠ **`go.work` is not committed** (it is in `.gitignore` by design, for the sibling-checkout workflow).
  The prototype's local run used one to point the generator at the module branch; CI and a fresh clone
  resolve the pin from `go.mod` with no workspace file, which is the configuration that must be green.
* ✔ **The pinned revision is merged.** `go.mod` pins `v0.0.0-20261011032322-3dc0e291e59d`, the merge
  commit of `QuarkLangQkparser#3` on the module's `main` — verified by resolving it through the Go
  toolchain after the merge, with the generated catalog unchanged by the repin. The order was load
  bearing (module first, then this repository's pin) and was done that way.
* ⚠ **CI wall-clock cost** of the generation check is unmeasured. It shells out to `go list -m`, which is
  cheap with a warm module cache and needs the module downloaded with a cold one — and the module is
  already a dependency, so a cold cache pays for it once either way.
